Terms for Official Instances

On most Trycord instances, the people you deal with are the people who run that instance. On an official instance, that is us. These terms cover the difference.

Operator action required. Items marked OPERATOR need the official operator's legal name, address, retention periods, and supervisory authority before these terms are presented to anyone.

1. What an official instance is

An official instance is a hosted Trycord instance operated by the Trycord project, or by a partner we have appointed and published. It is listed in the app. Being listed is the whole of the designation: there is no other certification, and no other instance may present itself as official.

Everything else — a community's own server, a friend's instance, a copy you host — is not official, even if it runs unmodified software.

2. How these terms relate to the main Terms

The Terms of Service Official instance terms apply to official instances too, and this page adds to them. Where the two conflict, these terms win. Nothing here removes a right you have under the main Terms.

3. Who runs it, and who you can contact

The operator is the Trycord project, contactable at OPERATOR: your contact address. Because one organisation operates every official instance, you do not have to work out who runs the one you joined: it is us, and there is one place to raise a problem.

This is the main practical difference. On a self-hosted instance, your only route for anything serious is that instance's operator. Here, you can reach the project directly.

4. Your data on an official instance

The operator is the data controller. The project sets and publishes the retention rules that apply across all official instances, so your data is not handled differently depending on which one you happened to join.

  • Retention: OPERATOR: your retention periods
  • Backups: OPERATOR: your backup schedule and retention
  • Hosting and subprocessors: OPERATOR: your hosting provider and subprocessors
  • Where data is stored: OPERATOR: the country or region your data is stored in
  • Your rights: access, correction, export, and erasure, as set out in the Privacy Policy

Export is the one we hold ourselves to most firmly. You should always be able to get your data out, in a usable format, without asking a favour. If that is ever hard on an official instance, treat it as a bug and report it as one.

5. Moderation on official instances

Official instances carry platform-wide rules that apply everywhere, because they are operated by one party. Beyond that, communities on an official instance set their own rules, and their own moderators enforce them, the same as anywhere else.

Because we operate every official instance, a report about enforcement can be raised centrally rather than only with a community you may already have been banned from. See Support for how to appeal.

6. Availability

Official instances are provided free of charge, and are offered on an as-available basis. We publish a status page, and we aim to be straightforward about incidents rather than quiet about them. We do not offer an uptime guarantee, and no paid tier changes that unless it is written down here.

7. Suspension on official instances

We may suspend accounts that break the Terms of Service or platform-wide rules. Because we operate the instance, we can see the context of a decision — including whether a community moderator acted correctly — and appeals are reviewed centrally.

We do not sell data, and we do not use your messages to train models. If that ever changes, it will be disclosed here and in the Privacy Policy before it happens, not after.

8. Ending an official instance

If an official instance is closed, we will publish notice on the status page, give reasonable time to export, and keep the export available for a defined period afterwards: OPERATOR: how long an export stays available after an instance closes. We will not silently delete communities that people are still using.

9. Liability

The limitations in section 11 of the Terms of Service apply here. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited, and where you are a consumer, the protections your local law gives you are unaffected.

10. Contact

OPERATOR: your address for formal notices · Start at Support for anything that is not a formal notice.
